newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile senate board approves Canada trade treaty.
newsitem.headline: Chile senate board approves Canada trade treaty.

text.p: A Chilean senate mixed commission has voted in favour of the free trade treaty with Canada which will be voted on by the whole senate July 1.

The commission, representing the foreign affairs, economy and agriculture panels, agreed 10 to 4, with one abstention, to recommend that the senate approve the deal which will phase out trade barriers between the two countries.
President Eduardo Frei and Prime Minister Jean Chretien signed the agreement last year.
The government welcomed the vote, which took place after long debates during which three ministers were questioned, as an important step towards the approval of the treaty by the Senate.
The vote was a "substantial advance and a positive result, as we had been expecting," said Finance Minister Eduardo Aninat.
"I'm leaving satisfied. I think the negotiating team and the three ministers who were involved have covered an enormous number of questions and we are now advancing to the next stage," said Aninat.
"(The process) is still not finished but this gives a very good signal."

Senators who voted in favour included congressmen from the ruling center-left coalition, two military-designated senators and one rightist congressman. The pact was opposed by other lawmakers from the right-wing opposition parties. Opposition congressmen were protesting over claims the government has not met its commitments to farmers agreed when Chile became an associate member of the Mercosur trade bloc last year.
The treaty must now be studied Wednesday by the senate's finance commission.
It was approved by the lower house of Congress in May
